historic/u3e1/george-grenville-portrait..description: Portrait of George Grenville (1712-1770) by William Hoare, 1764. Prime Minister 1763-1765, author of the Stamp Act.
historic/u3e1/george-grenville-portrait..fallback_note: Wikimedia Special:FilePath -> direct upload.wikimedia.org -> NYPL (different host) -> Commons redirect

historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-map.jpg.description: Map showing the Proclamation Line of 1763 running along the Appalachian Mountains. German-labeled version; the red line is the visual point.

historic/u3e1/proclamation-document.jpg.description: The Royal Proclamation of 1763 document, issued by George III after the French and Indian War.

historic/u3e1/pontiac.jpg.description: Artist's impression of Pontiac, Ottawa chief who led the 1763 rebellion against British forts.

historic/u3e1/fort-detroit-siege.jpg.description: The siege of Fort Detroit during Pontiac's Rebellion, 1763.

historic/u3e1/fort-pitt-plan.jpg.description: 1759 plan of Fort Pitt, where British officers distributed smallpox-infected blankets in 1763.

historic/u3e1/paxton-boys.jpg.description: The Paxton Boys marching on Philadelphia, 1764, after their 1763 attacks on Conestoga Indians.

historic/u3e1/edmund-burke.jpg.description: Edmund Burke, who coined the phrase 'salutary neglect' in his 1775 speech on conciliation with America.

historic/u3e1/british-troops.jpg.description: Benjamin West's 'The Death of General Wolfe' (1770) — iconic depiction of British troops in North America during the French and Indian War era.

historic/u3e1/french-indian-war.jpg.description: George Washington at the Battle of the Monongahela (1755) — the costly war that left Britain deeply in debt.

historic/u3e1/appalachian-mountains.jpg.description: The Appalachian Mountains, along which the Proclamation Line of 1763 ran.

historic/u3e1/jeffery-amherst-portrait.j.description: Portrait of General Jeffery Amherst, whose postwar policies helped provoke Pontiac's Rebellion.

historic/u3e1/edmund-burke-portrait.jpg.description: Portrait of Edmund Burke, who in 1775 coined the retrospective phrase 'salutary neglect' to describe a century of unenforced trade laws that ended after the Seven Years' War.

historic/u3e1/royal-proclamation-1763-do.description: Printed text of the Royal Proclamation of 1763 establishing British administration, reserving lands west of the Appalachians for Native nations and requiring license for trade - London's triage to avoid another costly frontier war.

historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-1763-map.description: Contemporary map showing the Proclamation Line along the crest of the Appalachians as the fence, with the Mississippi Valley as the prize, illustrating why the line 'came too late' and failed as a fence but stung as an insult to land speculators including Washington.

historic/u3e1/chief-pontiac-portrait.jpg.description: Portrait of Pontiac, Ottawa war chief around the Great Lakes who organized the 1763 pan-Indian alliance after the French defeat, distinct from Delaware prophet Neolin whose vision urged rejecting guns, alcohol, and infighting.
